questions.q: Which best describes a primary source in art research?
options: A biography of an artist from a website
A drawing you make in front of an original artwork
questions.why: Primary sources are first-hand: your own drawings, photos or seeing the original.

questions.q: What does AO1 ask you to show?
options: Develop ideas through investigations, demonstrating critical understanding of sources
Present a personal response with a neat finish
Use as many materials as possible
questions.why: This is the AO1 wording from the Pearson specification.

questions.q: Which sketchbook page would earn the highest AO1 credit?
options: A printed artist photo with a copied biography
A neat copy of a painting with no comment
Many pages with a different artist on each
A study of the artist's technique on your own subject, with analysis and a note on how it will influence your outcome
questions.why: Critical understanding means analysing, testing and linking the source to your own intentions.

questions.q: Explain how you would use an artist's work to develop your own idea, not just copy it.
questions.model: I would study how the artist works (technique, palette, composition), try the technique on my own subject, evaluate what worked, and use it deliberately in my final piece.
points: study/analyse the artist's technique or ideas
